content.comment_body: Hello, I would like to know if it’s possible to use the Message Text shown on the [product_name] Operator Device as a condition to change a setpoint. Specifically, if I am viewing one page on the device, I want to change one setpoint using the cursor keys, and if I see another page, I want to change a different setpoint with the same keys. Is this possible? If yes, how can it be done? Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, Yes, this is possible. When you activate a message, the output of the block will be 1. You can use this output as a condition in your program. If you need further details, please let us know. Regards,

I may not have explained my situation clearly. In my program, I start two different motors, each producing a Message Text. My intention was to be able to scroll between these Message Texts and, while one page is selected, to change a setpoint using the available keys.
Hello, You could check [url] for application examples related to [product_name]. There is an example for menu control with the Operator Device, which should cover what you are looking for. Regards,
This isn't exactly what I was thinking, but it is still very helpful!

analysis.insight_summary: A user wants to adjust different setpoints based on the message or page currently displayed on a [product_name] Operator Device, using the same hardware keys. Other community members provided clarifications and suggestions, mentioning the use of message activation outputs and referencing product application examples. The user found the support useful even though the solution differed somewhat from their initial idea.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to use the active message displayed on the [product_name] Operator Device to enable context-dependent setpoint adjustments with the same keys.
